title: Isosceles-free sets in the triangular grid
statement: Let the triangular grid T_N be the points a + b w (w = e^(i pi/3)) with integers a, b >= 0 and a + b <= N - 1, N(N+1)/2 points forming a triangle of side N - 1 in the Eisenstein lattice; the squared distance between two of them is da^2 + da db + db^2. Determine the largest number of points of the triangular grid T_N such that no point is equidistant from two others (no isosceles triangle, flat ones included: no point is the midpoint of two others), as a function of N. The exact values are known (ours) for N <= 10; the headline cell is N = 14: find 15 or more such points of the region of side 14 (an upper bound is 53).
submission: Text file: one point 'a b' per line, a point of the region of side 14 (lines starting with # are ignored).
score: the number of points (larger is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 14 points of the region of side 14 with no point equidistant from two others (no isosceles triangle, flat ones included), the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)

context: A set of points is isosceles-free when no point of it is equidistant from two others: no three of its points form an isosceles triangle, counting the flat case of a point midway between two others. For the n x n square grid the largest such sets have become a test bed for machine-assisted constructions: PatternBoost (Charton, Ellenberg, Wagner and Williamson, 2024) and AlphaEvolve (Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner, 2025) found sets of 108 to 112 points in the 64 x 64 grid, the first values are OEIS A271907, and the best lower bound proved, of order n sqrt(log log n / log n) (arXiv:2610.04194, 2026), is far from the subquadratic upper bounds (the grid question is Erdos problem #1207). In the triangular (Eisenstein) lattice every interior point has six neighbours at the same distance, every equilateral triangle is isosceles, and the squared distances are the Loschian numbers a^2 + ab + b^2, so equal distances are frequent and the extremal sets are sparse. The exact values grow roughly like N (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 for N = 2..10); whether the growth stays linear, and at what rate, is open.
references: F. Charton, J. S. Ellenberg, A. Z. Wagner, G. Williamson, PatternBoost: constructions in mathematics with a little help from AI, arXiv:2411.00566 (2024)
B. Georgiev, J. Gomez-Serrano, T. Tao, A. Z. Wagner, Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale, arXiv:2511.02864 (2025)
Sparse coloring for isosceles-free grids: an AI-assisted proof case study, arXiv:2610.04194 (2026)
OEIS A271907 (largest subsets of the n x n grid with no isosceles triangle)

novelty.verdict: new question for this lattice: isosceles-free subsets are studied for the n x n square grid (OEIS A271907, PatternBoost, AlphaEvolve, arXiv:2610.04194); no result was found for the triangular grid, and its first values are not in the OEIS as such (the first ten agree with the sums of three squares, A000378, by coincidence; the value 13 for N = 11 already differs).
closest: The n x n square grid (OEIS A271907; PatternBoost arXiv:2411.00566; AlphaEvolve arXiv:2511.02864; arXiv:2610.04194): the same question in another lattice.
Erdos-type questions on isosceles sets in the plane and in space: point sets in which every three points form an isosceles triangle, the opposite extreme.

baseline.text: 14 for N = 14, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: the points in `refs/tri-isosceles.txt` (the best set CP-SAT found in 10 seconds, started from the set for side N - 1 (tools/lattice_sets.py)). Exact values for N = 2..10: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 (CP-SAT (OR-Tools 9.15, one worker) proved the optimum of the 0/1 model in tools/lattice_sets.py). Upper bound for N = 14: 53 (every chosen point sees the others at different distances, and no point of the region sees more than 52 different distances).
